title: Automated segmentation and radiomics stratify risk in serous ovarian cancer
summary: An end-to-end pipeline combined U-Net-based automated segmentation of primary ovarian cancer lesions on contrast-enhanced CT with radiomics and machine learning survival models, in 607 retrospectively collected scans. Segmentation Dice scores were 0.90, 0.88 and 0.80 across validation and two test sets; the best radiomics model had C-index 0.66 (validation), 0.72 (TCIA) and 0.60 (KEM). It improved risk stratification over CA-125, residual disease and FIGO stage in the authors' comparison. Retrospective; preprint of 2023-04-28.
ai_technology: U-Net-based automated segmentation plus radiomics with 13 feature reduction methods and 12 machine learning algorithms for survival prediction

evidence.tested: External test sets from TCIA (n=73) and Kliniken Essen-Mitte (n=323).
evidence.unknown: Prospective validation, clinical benefit and peer-reviewed status are not established; C-indices are moderate; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning segmented tumors and machine learning models predicted survival from radiomic features.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations were not available. Publisher full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
